correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the dihedral automorphism averaging argument using the convex centered operator norm, valid for all noninvariant feasible matrices. For invariant weights a,b, 2a+b<=1, diagonalization along the ring yields eigenvalues 1-b-a delta ±sqrt(b²+a²delta²), delta=1-cos(2pi j/n). For r=u²=1-cos(2pi/n), the positive-mode lower envelope strictly decreases in a and has a strictly convex unique b optimizer: a=(u+2)/(2H), b=u(u+1)/H, H=u²+2u+2. Check negative modes using mu²-[b²+(1-b)²]=u(u+2)(2-u²)/H²>0 for n>=3; mu=2(u+1)/H is actually attained as SLEM. At a=b=1/3 heuristic mu=(2-u²+sqrt(1+u^4))/3, optimal/heuristic gap tends to 3/2. Independent matrix eigenvalue experiments at all n=3..50 reproduce both; proof is all-mode analytical and not extrapolated.
residual_risks: Computational examples alone do not establish quantification beyond checked finite parameters; the analytical or finite-exhaustive proof is separately evaluated.

value.rationale: Sunlets form a natural infinite bounded-degree graph family with slow ring mixing. Exact optimum edge weights, all-eigenmode attainment, and a 50% limiting gap advantage over standard heuristics are useful analytic mixing benchmarks; the result is not merely a numerical SDP instance.
residual_risks: Downstream use is plausible but not asserted as a published external application; value rests on the motivated mathematical claim itself.
